claim: For the Blakaj--Wolf anisotropic XY family, set \(H_0=\sigma_x\otimes\sigma_x+\sigma_y\otimes\sigma_y\) and \(H_1=-\sigma_x\otimes\sigma_x+\sigma_y\otimes\sigma_y\), and let \[\mathcal C=\{(a,b):a=\operatorname{tr}(\rho H_1),\ b=\operatorname{tr}(\rho H_0),\ \rho\in\operatorname{Red}_2\}.\] Near the lower-boundary point exposed by \(H_0\), the boundary of \(\mathcal C\) is a graph \(b=g(a)\) with \(g(0)=-1/(4\pi)\). It is \(C^2\) but not \(C^3\) at \(a=0\), and its graph curvature vanishes logarithmically: \[g''(a)\sim\frac{4\pi}{\log(1/|a|)}\qquad(a\to0).\] Equivalently, the support function \(\epsilon(\gamma)=\min_{(a,b)\in\mathcal C}(b+\gamma a)\) has \[\epsilon(\gamma)=-\frac1{4\pi}-\frac{\gamma^2}{8\pi}\left(\log\frac4{|\gamma|}-\frac12\right)-\frac{3\gamma^4}{64\pi}\left(\log\frac4{|\gamma|}-\frac{13}{12}\right)+O\!\left(\gamma^6\log\frac1{|\gamma|}\right).\] Thus \(\epsilon\) is \(C^1\) but not \(C^2\) at \(\gamma=0\), correcting the analyticity assertion in Theorem 3 of arXiv:2308.14585. The same logarithmic term also gives a local proof of the paper's non-semialgebraicity theorem: semialgebraicity would make \(\epsilon\) piecewise algebraic, while Newton--Puiseux expansions cannot contain a nonzero \(\gamma^2\log|\gamma|\) term.
integrity: The proof uses the exact source support function, the convergent DLMF endpoint expansion, exact Legendre duality, and Newton--Puiseux theory. Finite numerical checks are corroborative only.
scientific_limitations: The theorem concerns the explicitly defined two-observable projection of \(\operatorname{Red}_2\), not the full reduced-state set.
The graph-coordinate second derivative \(g''\) is not an affine-invariant curvature.
The elliptic asymptotic and physical anisotropy transition are prior knowledge; originality is limited to the reduced-state boundary law, theorem correction, and local semialgebraicity obstruction.
title: Logarithmic flattening of the XY support boundary of translation-invariant reduced states
